corrections.reason: The description and the A6.12 expectation both include compare stories ("Who has more? By how much?"). A kid cannot solve those without understanding more and less, and no other listed prerequisite (k-add-sub-facts-5 depends only on k-make-numbers-to-10) provides that, so k-more-less-same is a missing direct prerequisite.

corrections.description: Name Canadian coins and bills. Tell how much each is worth, up to 25 cents for coins and 10 dollars for bills.
corrections.reason: The symbols 25¢ and $10 do not read aloud reliably. Spelling out "25 cents" and "10 dollars" suits a kid hearing the description read aloud and keeps the same meaning.

corrections.description: Match numerals from 0 to 20 to groups of things, and write the number you see.
corrections.reason: The A6.3 expectation is to identify and write numbers to 20. The description says "type", which describes a different activity and does not match the expectation. Changing it to "write" aligns the description with the expectation.

output.notes: I checked all 13 Kindergarten skills for needed, direct, and missing prerequisites, for pointers to later grades or to themselves, and for title and description fit. No prerequisite is redundant: no listed prerequisite depends on another listed one, and there are no cycles or forward references. All prerequisite ids exist in the prompt. Counting-based prerequisites (k-count-to-20 in k-more-less-same and k-equal-share) are left as is, since counting is the expected strategy at this grade and the link is defensible. The k-make-numbers-to-10 title is narrower than its description but is not wrong, so I did not change it.
